contract.rows: Array under the key 'rows', one object per application.

keys.id: channel.application, lowercase, unique, for example instagram.portrait
keys.channel: website, substack, email, x, threads, instagram, youtube, tiktok, linkedin, video, print, slides
keys.width, height: Numbers in 'unit'. Either may be null where the platform states only one side or none
keys.aspect: Width to height as the platform writes it, such as '1.91:1' or '4:5', or null
keys.formats: Lowercase file types the platform accepts, or null where it states none
keys.max_bytes: File size limit in bytes, decimal (1 MB = 1,000,000), or null
keys.safe_area: null, or an object: {'type': 'insets', 'top', 'right', 'bottom', 'left'} in the row's unit, with an optional 'exclude' list of boxes {'x', 'y', 'width', 'height'} measured from the top left that must also stay clear; {'type': 'box', 'width', 'height'} centered; {'type': 'circle', 'radius_pct'} centered, as a percent of the width
keys.smallest_shown_px: The smallest size, in CSS px, at which the platform's own page says it shows the item, or null where the page does not say
keys.match: exact (the export must be this size), min (this size or larger, same ratio), max (this size or smaller), or ratio (any size at the aspect)
keys.basis: platform (the platform states the figure) or studio-choice (the studio sets the figure, inside any platform limits the note names)
keys.note: Plain words on anything a script should not assume
keys.bleed: Print rows only: the bleed on each side, in inches. width and height are the trim size. A PDF passes when its TrimBox equals the trim size and its BleedBox (or MediaBox) equals the trim plus twice the bleed (8.75 x 11.25 in for Letter). Null on every other row

contract.check: A dimension script compares an export's pixel or page size to width and height by 'match'. Rows with status other than 'read' still check, and the script should print their status beside the result so a reader sees which figures rest on a search result.
